title: SharePoint: Viva Connections multi-home site management moves to the SharePoint admin center
summary: The briefing's migration, licensing, default state and qualified PowerShell guidance are supported by Microsoft's documentation and notice. Minor corrections should extend the add-home-site route and remove the checklist's unrepresented site-permissions control.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Viva Connections multi-home site management is moving from the Microsoft 365 admin center to the SharePoint admin center.
claims.quote: Viva Connections multi-home site management is moving from the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) to the SharePoint Admin Center (SPAC).

claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators will create and manage multiple home sites in the SharePoint admin center.
claims.quote: Administrators will be able to create and manage multiple Home sites

claims.claim: The roadmap says audience targeting configuration moves to the SharePoint admin center.
claims.quote: configure audience targeting, manage home site priority order, and remove Home sites directly from SPAC.

claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators will manage home site priority order in the SharePoint admin center.
claims.quote: manage home site priority order, and remove Home sites directly from SPAC.

claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators will remove home sites in the SharePoint admin center.
claims.quote: remove Home sites directly from SPAC.

claims.claim: Existing Microsoft 365 admin center entry points will redirect administrators to the new SharePoint admin center experience.
claims.quote: Existing entry points in the Microsoft 365 admin center will direct administrators to the new SPAC experience.

claims.claim: Home sites can be created or added at SharePoint admin center > Settings > Home sites > Add.
claims.quote:
Select Settings, and then select Home sites.
Select Add, and then select Create a new site.
Preview the Home site template, and then select Use template.
claims.fix: The printed route stops at the correct wizard entry. Extend controls[0].ui.path to 'Settings > Home sites > Add > Create a new site > Use template > Create site'. Add to its note: 'For an existing site, use Settings > Home sites > Add > Use an existing communication site.' These routes are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/homesites/set-up-admin-center.

claims.claim: Set-SPOHomeSite -HomeSiteUrl <site URL> sets a site as a home site, with the row expressly qualifying its multi-home-site limitations.
claims.quote:
Sets a SharePoint Site as a Home Site.
Set-SPOHomeSite
    -HomeSiteUrl <String>
Sets the URL of the site collection to be the home site.

claims.claim: Audience editing is at SharePoint admin center > Settings > Home sites > home site > three dots menu > Edit audience.
claims.quote:
In Settings > Home sites, select the home site.
Select the three dots menu (...), and then select Edit audience.

claims.claim: Home site priority is edited at SharePoint admin center > Settings > Home sites > Change order.
claims.quote:
In Settings > Home sites, select Change order.
Drag home sites into the order you want.

claims.claim: Removal is at SharePoint admin center > Settings > Home sites > home site > three dots menu > Remove as home site.
claims.quote:
In Settings > Home sites, select the three dots menu (...) for a home site.
Select Remove as home site. A confirmation panel opens.

claims.claim: Remove-SPOHomeSite removes the current home site setting, with the row expressly qualifying its multi-home-site limitations.
claims.quote:
Removes the current SharePoint Online Home site setting.
Remove-SPOHomeSite

claims.claim: The management migration arrives automatically without administrator action, supporting defaultState on.
claims.quote: your existing home sites, audiences, and order appear in the SharePoint admin center automatically. You don't need to do anything to move them.

claims.claim: Licensing is mixed: the Microsoft 365 entitlement covers one experience, while multiple experiences require a Viva licence.
claims.quote:
Users with a Microsoft 365 subscription (E, F, or A license) are limited to creating and using one experience.
If you want to create or use two or more experiences (up to 50), then every user in your tenant must have a Microsoft Viva Suite or Viva Communications and Communities license.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state the specific treatment or subsequent visibility of draft-state experiences during the automatic upgrade.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Viva Connections" "draft" "upgraded" "September"' and '"Viva Connections" "multi-home" "draft" migration'; read MC1457839 and the full setup page. Automatic upgrade is stated, but no draft-specific migration or visibility rule is given.

claims.where: Governance controls: PowerShell paragraph; Open questions

claims.quote: Searched: '"SharePoint" "home site" "DraftMode" "retired"'; read Set-SPOHomeSite, set-up-admin-center and MC1457839. The reference lists DraftMode, but no transition or parameter-retirement rule is stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document whether the existing home site cmdlets now add or remove entries in the new multi-home-site management list.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint home sites audience priority order PowerShell Microsoft Graph Set-SPOHomeSite multiple DraftMode migration'; read setup, Set-SPOHomeSite and Remove-SPOHomeSite. Initial limitations are given, but post-migration multi-site support is not stated.
